quest.title: The Eternal Dream, Ever Lush
quest.description: Finally, you have arrived at the unchanging, eternal oasis, and thus is a great weight lifted off Jeht's shoulders...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x150, Primogem x20, Mora x25000, Adventure EXP x150, Primogem x20, Unknown Item #28432 x1, Mora x25000, Adventure EXP x150, Primogem x20, Mora x35000

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow... Paimon didn't think that a place like this could exist in the desert...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? Was the sun already going down when we first came out from underground?

dialogues.speaker: Liloupar
dialogues.text: No... This is my mistress' paradise, a place frozen at the point where the sky kisses the waters, where ingenuity and devotion comingle. The resultant here and now, then, is named eternity.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow... Paimon understood almost none of that, but it's why nothing moves here, right?

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Is this why my parents regarded this place as their final destination?

dialogues.speaker: Liloupar
dialogues.text: Those are not my words... *sigh* Interpret this however you will, poor child...

talks.objective: Go to where the Goddess of Flowers slumbers

dialogues.speaker: Liloupar
dialogues.text: My mistress... She is not here.

dialogues.speaker: Liloupar
dialogues.text: Instead, here is another fragment of myself...

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: As the shard of light merges with Liloupar's magic bottle, you feel a little of your own power being pulled away... But a warmth then quickly fills you.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text:
Through the Jinni's entranced eyes, you see a palace shaped by bricks of crimson jade bound to a garden, flourishing with a multiplicity of vibrant plants that bask in infinite bird-song.
The Jinn are the most intelligent servants of the Mistress of Flowers, and to her they are minstrels and cupbearers both.
In her garden, addled monks and ragged wanderers dance, spiraling in step with the daffodils, supping the lifeblood of the daughters of the vine...
Here is a garden unlike any other, the place where the Lord of Flowers once lived, the place where she now sleeps...

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: "The roses blossom like crackling flames, setting the lives of nocturnal birds aflame. And though the candles smile gently, they offer the approaching moths only ruin."

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You see her reach out and behold her skin gleaming with lunar sheen. You gaze upon her mien and witness ineffable beauty. Her appearance is like the totality of her Jinn, their wondrous aspects only mere petals to her complete flower, her being the quintessence to every last scent in existence...\nAnd then, you meet her gaze—

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: And face nothingness.\nYou greet the endless void, falling into its embrace, mind afire with constant terror...

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: As your consciousness clears, you find Jeht clutching your hand, her expression clouded with concern.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: You're awake... How are you feeling?

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: You just... *sigh* Never mind. The important thing is that you're alright...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What... What did you see? You look like you just woke up from a long and scary dream...

choices.text: I saw the Mistress of Flowers...

response.speaker: Liloupar
response.text: She is gone. He lied to us. He lied to us all.

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: What do you mean?

response.speaker: Liloupar
response.text: It's nothing — just the cancellation of an ancient pact. I believe I'm... finally free?

response.speaker: Liloupar
response.text: The Lord of the Sands once swore to us that our Mistress of Flowers slumbered here, destined to awake someday. But...

response.speaker: Liloupar
response.text: How strange. Our mistress has already passed. He... He deceived me. He deceived my people.

response.speaker: Liloupar
response.text: I should feel maddening hatred for him right now. For this desert. For the death of my mistress... My loathing should have matched the love and admiration I once held for him...

response.speaker: Liloupar
response.text: Yet, I find myself empty of want or will to hate... How odd...

choices.text: Maybe this is what it means to be free.

response.speaker: Liloupar
response.text: Is that so...

response.speaker: Liloupar
response.text: Hmph, spare me the niceties. My master you remain, and our pact endures yet.

response.speaker: Liloupar
response.text: Come. Let us depart. Jeht was waiting for you this whole time, you know.

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: Y'know what? I see a nice spot just over there. I'm going to head over first.

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: Don't forget to come over in a bit.

choices.text: You are now neither bound to "lovers" nor "foes."
I gazed upon this place as it appeared long ago...

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: This place should be it... It matches the sketches in my mother's journal.

dialogues.speaker: Liloupar
dialogues.text: A fine place for a restful slumber, no?

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: ...Yeah.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: We've faced countless dangers in our trek across this desert: betrayals, plots... Unforgivable wrongs, incomprehensible events... All in quick succession too...

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: But here, I feel calm... Happy. I don't know why. I just do.

dialogues.speaker: Liloupar
dialogues.text: It is because this place is the Mistress of Flowers' final sphere of influence... The offerings of the skies protect its serenity here, deep beneath the earth. Thus does this place preserve the last of her essence...

dialogues.speaker: Liloupar
dialogues.text: And though she is long gone, this place remains as calm as it was at its inception, as if it was never disturbed. Hence, those who arrive in this place... will know only peace and joy.

dialogues.speaker: Liloupar
dialogues.text: For the mistress was once the guardian of maddened monks and lost wanderers. To them, this place was indeed a paradise they could call home.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Jeht quietly sets her mother's notes down and lays Jebrael's axe by its side...\nNow, it is as if they were never parted.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Sorry... I'm just at a loss for words right now.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: It's like... time forgot how to flow and everything stopped. I don't know why. I can't even gasp in astonishment at all that's around me here because... All I feel is peace.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: For my parents to slumber here alongside our fallen goddess... Though I wish they had never left...

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: I truly wish that they could stay here eternally, never to be forgotten by the passing of time.

dialogues.speaker: Liloupar
dialogues.text: When we first entered, we disrupted the fragment's power and broke the device that long maintained equilibrium here... This place is destined for ruin, to be swallowed by the sands sooner or later.

dialogues.speaker: Liloupar
dialogues.text: When that time comes, the fading power that our mistress put forth to ward this oasis in perpetuity will dissipate... This is inevitable.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: I know that. But at least my parents were reunited before the end, as if they'd never left each other at all.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Maybe there will finally come a day when I return to this place. After I grow weary of adventuring, and after I have left every place I regard to be "home" behind.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: At that point, I think I'll just say: "I'm back!" and then lay between my parents to join them for a grand old nap.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Jeht... But that day's still far, far away! Right now Jebrael is probably happily... um, not-smiling, because his face is always blank. But Paimon's sure he's happy...

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Thanks, Paimon...

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: #And you too, {NICKNAME}. Thanks for walking this path with me, and for fulfilling this willful, cherished desire of mine... But I'd like to have a bit of alone-time with my parents...

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: Yes... Thank you.

choices.text: Don't forget to come back to us, alright?

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: Don't worry about me... I'll catch up. Ha. I mean, it isn't my time to settle down here yet, is it?

dialogues.speaker: Liloupar
dialogues.text: She is a good child, my master.

dialogues.speaker: Liloupar
dialogues.text: Though born to beastly brutality and slight of wit, her survival instincts are astute beyond compare...

dialogues.speaker: Liloupar
dialogues.text: She perceives who it is who wishes to see her hurt, and upon sensing such intent, she gives her all to retaliate without mercy, regardless of how much intimacy may lie between...

dialogues.speaker: Liloupar
dialogues.text: Still... She does not know the schemes woven against her. She does not yet know that the home she seeks... is a thing most hollow.

dialogues.speaker: Liloupar
dialogues.text: Master, if you care for her, then protect her well.

dialogues.speaker: Liloupar
dialogues.text: A mere suggestion on my part, of course. You may take it to be... I do not know. Perhaps you might consider it the unworthy atonement of one who was once a mother...

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: (There she sits in silence, enjoying a pleasant time with her parents.)

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: If you don't mind, I'd like to stay a while longer... If that's okay with you, I mean.

choices.text: The tribe is waiting on us.

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: Yeah... Just... Give me some more time.

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: You go. I'll follow after.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: I feel much better now. Thanks.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Are you sure you're fine? You can rest more if you want...

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Let's head back. We need to tell Matriarch Babel about the details of our journey.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Alright, if you say so... Then, let's go!

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: We're back and intact, Matriarch Babel.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: We have discovered the secrets of the Eternal Oasis, and opened the path there for the tribe.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: I... Thank you for this opportunity. To help me fulfill my parents' dreams... Even if they didn't receive the blessings of the Tanit.

dialogues.speaker: Babel
dialogues.text: Please, child, there's no need. I have always held your hopes close to my heart. To be able to fulfill the desires of the young is my duty as Matriarch.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Thank you...

dialogues.speaker: Babel
dialogues.text: Well done, Jeht. Now, there is the matter of Azariq...

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Your judgment was accurate... He's undoubtedly a traitor.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, so you already knew that Azariq would betray you?

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: No. I only suspected him at first, and spent most of the journey watching him... I just didn't expect him to reveal his true intent so soon.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Matriarch Babel warned me, but I chose to believe him at the time.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Here: proof of his collusion with the Fatui.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Jeht gives Aderfi's letter to Babel.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Please don't be sad, Matriarch Babel...

dialogues.speaker: Babel
dialogues.text: Yes... I long-suspected his disloyalty. It is just a shame that I didn't get the chance to end him personally... And I had such high hopes for him, too.

dialogues.speaker: Babel
dialogues.text: But now, with the tribe facing increasingly treacherous circumstances, and the loss of two individuals I invested much time and effort in, I must count on you, Jeht, to help me in matters both great and small going forward.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So... What you're saying is that Jeht got a promotion? Yeah! Congratulations, Jeht!

dialogues.speaker: Babel
dialogues.text: Promotion? Haha... That's not a word you hear in the desert very often.

dialogues.speaker: Babel
dialogues.text: We desert-dwellers aren't so hierarchical. In the end, they who govern more affairs will be the ones to bear greater authority.

dialogues.speaker: Babel
dialogues.text: Jeht... The future of the Tanit now rests on your shoulders. Don't let the tribe down.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Tribe... So, you're saying I'm truly one of the Tanit now?

dialogues.speaker: Babel
dialogues.text: Do not be deceived, child. I have always seen you as one of us. Whatever happened before, you are a daughter of the Tanit, and the truth of our consanguinity will always run in your veins.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: I... Thank you.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm, Paimon feels like we've forgotten to mention some suspicious things we saw...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, do you remember seeing anything suspicious?

choices.text: About the abandoned camps in the canyon...

response.speaker: Liloupar
response.text: You once dispatched other tribespeople into the oasis and left them to perish there. Then, you laid a taboo upon it as a pretext to prevent anyone else from trespassing, did you not?

response.speaker: Liloupar
response.text: Yet, you encouraged us to head deeper into that same treacherous territory, mentioning nothing of your actions. Why did you do this?

response.speaker: Babel
response.text: Esteemed Liloupar, allow me to offer my deepest apologies for all the inconveniences and misunderstandings you must have experienced.

response.speaker: Babel
response.text: But you are right. We have been exploring the ruins of Gurabad and the Eternal Oasis for quite some time... I sent many people from the tribe there in times past.

response.speaker: Babel
response.text: That we learned these few key locations and the general layout of the area is all thanks to their efforts...

response.speaker: Babel
response.text: Yet, due to the extreme danger of the missions, a vast majority of those brave explorers never returned, and the efforts from these expeditions bore scarce fruit.

response.speaker: Babel
response.text: Hence, I put a stop to the forays and marked entry into the place as taboo.

response.speaker: Babel
response.text: The traitor, Azariq, once led teams to survey the canyon and the ruins, and so I thought I could trust him to serve as your guide. I did not initially think that he would turn on us...

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: You... never spoke of this.

response.speaker: Babel
response.text: Because I knew from the start that you would return unharmed. Of all who inherit our legacy, you are the one I trust the most, Jeht.

response.speaker: Babel
response.text: Your fearlessness, your fierceness, your cunning, along with the gentleness and sincerity with which you treat your tribe and friends... They have not gone unnoticed.

response.speaker: Babel
response.text: If my daughter had not been stolen from me by the sands, I like to think that she might've turned out to be like you. Unflinching in the face of all peril, one whom even the desert could not smother...

response.speaker: Babel
response.text: So I believed in you and prayed for you in silence.

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: ...I'm sorry for doubting you, Matriarch Babel.

response.speaker: Babel
response.text: No. The fault is mine for incurring your doubt and mistrust. It is I who should ask for forgiveness instead.

response.speaker: Liloupar
response.text: My apologies as well, my master. It seems that my paranoia got the best of me.

response.speaker: Babel
response.text: #Well, it is good that we all managed to clear the air between us. You are our honored guest, {NICKNAME}, and the Tanit will always welcome you.

response.speaker: Babel
response.text: Esteemed Master of the Jinni, whatever you may desire, I will do my utmost to fulfill, if you would only ask.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Anything?

response.speaker: Babel
response.text: Anything.

choices.text: I'd like to be compensated in Mora.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah! Mora! Mora! That's what we want!

response.speaker: Babel
response.text: Very well, you have earned it indeed. And... I thank you for taking care of Jeht for me.

response.speaker: Babel
response.text: Alright, don't let us keep you much longer. Again, I thank you for your help, O Master of the Jinni... May it not be long before you visit us again.

response.speaker: Babel
response.text: After all, we will need your guidance... and Liloupar's also.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What? We're not going for Mora?

response.speaker: Babel
response.text: Your friendship with the Tanit is indeed worthy of memorialization. Please accept our meager gift — I hope you shall keep it close to you, never to be discarded.

choices.text: Just offer a toast on my behalf at Jeht's birthday celebration.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah! And don't forget to offer one on Paimon's behalf, too!

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: Eh? Thank you...

response.speaker: Babel
response.text: Oh? Is this one of your outsider traditions, then? Very well...

response.speaker: Babel
response.text: I will bear your good intentions in your stead, then.

response.speaker: Liloupar
response.text: In Azariq and Aderfi's correspondence, it was mentioned that the reason they turned traitor was because you showed favoritism toward Jeht, who is a traitor's daughter in their eyes, and wanted her to serve as inheritor to your duties...

response.speaker: Liloupar
response.text: Aside from that, you also seem to be actively culling those who work with those you call the "northerners." Yet, you once relied on these very same traitors to strike deals with said northerners.

response.speaker: Liloupar
response.text: Now, the jargon of your people eludes my understanding, but I am curious as to what the words you just spoke meant.

response.speaker: Babel
response.text: Esteemed Liloupar, allow me to offer my deepest apologies for all the inconveniences and misunderstandings you must have experienced.

response.speaker: Babel
response.text: But the survival and prosperity of the Tanit can only be sustained through multilateral trade. That includes those who hail from the north.

response.speaker: Babel
response.text: Preoccupied as I was by a multitude of matters surrounding the tribe, I was unable to foresee the treachery these northerners harbored...

response.speaker: Babel
response.text: Later, I would discover that the dangers they represented far outweighed the benefits they offered... But by then, I could only take to removing the traitors within our tribe that had turned to them first.

response.speaker: Babel
response.text: This is also why I needed Jeht. Her ability to swiftly and efficiently cleanse the tribe of traitors is unmatched. Additionally, I deeply appreciate her loyalty and capability.

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: You... never spoke of this.

response.speaker: Babel
response.text: Because I knew from the start that you would return unharmed. Of all who inherit our legacy, you are the one I trust the most, Jeht.

response.speaker: Babel
response.text: Your fearlessness, your fierceness, your cunning, along with the gentleness and sincerity with which you treat your tribe and friends... They have not gone unnoticed.

response.speaker: Babel
response.text: If my daughter had not been stolen from me by the sands, I like to think that she might've turned out to be like you. Unflinching in the face of all peril, one whom even the desert could not smother...

response.speaker: Babel
response.text: So I believed in you and prayed for you in silence.

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: ...I'm sorry for doubting you, Matriarch Babel.

response.speaker: Babel
response.text: No. The fault is mine for incurring your doubt and mistrust. It is I who should ask for forgiveness instead.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: (There she sits in silence, enjoying a pleasant time with her parents.)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Best not to bother her.)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: No. Nothing right now.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: After pacing for a while, you decide to leave this oasis of stillness.\nSoon, Jeht catches up with you.
